current.descent_text: From the top of P6 (the anchor is unequipped at the true summit — P7 is a short scramble with no rappel anchor), rappel the bolted line: 6 single-rope rappels, or 3 double-rope rappels with a 60m rope for the longest one. Some parties instead go down the South Face, rappelling its line to Pineapple Pass.

current.rappels: Most parties scramble the North Ridge to the true summit and descend the South Face rappel line: 4 single-rope rappels on a 60 m rope to Pineapple Pass. Alternatively, rappel Indentured Servant from its bolted anchors with a 60 m rope.
current.rappel_count_note: Four rappels on a single 60 m rope used doubled, each under 30 m, reversing the four pitches back to Pineapple Pass - this is what almost every party does and how the stations are spaced. Two 60 m ropes let you link them into fewer, longer rappels. One 60 m rappel in the sequence comes up just short of the next tree, leaving a short unroped downscramble, which an added pitch-3 anchor now avoids. A separate, partly hidden bolted line beside pitches 1 and 2 exists so that ascending and descending parties are not in the same place; it is a different set of anchors, not a variation. Below Pineapple Pass the east gully holds two more bolted chain stations for two further rappels on a 60 m - optional, and many parties scramble out instead; there is meaningful rockfall hazard in that gully. Do not scramble directly up to Pineapple Pass on the way in: that ground is the rappel route.

rappel_detail.pull: Decide which side you are pulling from before the last climber leaves, and keep both strands clear of the clefts.

A second, partly hidden set of bolts sits off to the side of pitches 1 and 2 so descending parties do not have to share ground with climbers. It is a different line, and it needs a small swing climber's-right at the bottom to put your feet on the ground; continuing along the ramp there creates rope drag that makes the pull difficult

current.descent_text: From the top of P5, clip one more bolt and continue onto the North Ridge for roughly 100m of scrambling to the true summit. From there, most parties descend via the South Face's established rappel line (4 raps) back to Pineapple Pass; alternatively, rappel back down Indentured Servant itself with a 60m rope from the bolted anchors.

current.descent_text: Most parties reverse the South Face itself: four rappels straight back down the face to Pineapple Pass on a single 60m rope (used doubled — each rappel comes in under 30m). The stations are natural anchors kept well equipped with fixed slings, cord and rap rings: from the top down, a station with three rap rings backed by slings/cord around a tree or horn, then an 8mm doubled cordelette with two quicklinks, then two slung trees, then a lowest station with several slings and three rap rings around a block. A second, less-crowded rappel line exists on the southwest side with bolted chain-and-ring anchors, built specifically so ascending and descending parties don't have to share the same gully — also doable on a single 60m rope in a similar number of rappels. Once back at Pineapple Pass, the safest and most common way out is to skip further rappelling and simply reverse the Class 3–4 scramble and talus/snow descent through Great Scott Bowl back to the Source Lake junction on the Snow Lake Trail, then walk the 2 miles out to Alpental — this avoids rockfall exposure and is usually faster for parties larger than two. A separate bail option drops climbers from Pineapple Pass down the East Gully via two rappels off bolted chain anchors (single 60m rope) directly toward the Source Lake basin, but that gully sees rockfall from above and from parties climbing up it, so it's generally treated as an emergency/bail line rather than the standard way down. The moat/snow bridge at the base of the pass can again be the crux of the whole descent in early season — downclimb carefully or detour onto rock.

current.descent_text: Reverse the ascent line off the North Peak summit. Parties describe two to three rappels getting back down through the 4th/low-5th-class chimney-and-ramp section to easier 3rd-class ground above the glacier — plan on a single 60m rope (or two ropes if parties want to link stations in fewer pulls). The first rappel station is commonly an old fixed sling/tat anchor left by previous parties, but it should not be trusted blindly — inspect it or back it up, and be prepared to build natural gear anchors (cams/nuts on horns or cracks) for the remaining stations since fixed gear is inconsistent year to year. After the rappels, downclimb/scramble the remaining 3rd-class terrain back to the col, reverse the ~1,000 ft descent to the glacier, re-cross the Queest-Alb Glacier (watch the moat and any crevasses), climb back up to Tin Can Gap, and reverse Trail #641 through Goat Flats and Saddle Lake to the trailhead. Rockfall in the chimney/gully and a icy glacier moat are the main descent-specific hazards; a mid-to-late-season descent in soft/rotten snow on the glacier headwall can also be tricky.
